rationale: One unblinded trial randomized 80 students and reports a favorable menstrual-weakness contrast for fennel soft capsules. An independent extraction reports 38 analyzed controls. Other fatigue results range from inconclusive comparisons to an author abstract for fixed-order fennel-drop treatment. Differences in preparation and population keep the inverse lean at the minimal tier.

The concentrated pepper extract experiment, leaf-tea comparison and botanical mixtures do not isolate consumed ground peppercorns in Parkinson insomnia. The reported intranasal pepper-and-honey remedy remains a secondary attribution because the original remedy table is unavailable. No eligible direction is established.

Cooked brown rice and related feed experiments give a favorable timed-climbing signal in iron-exposed flies. Matched wild-type brown-versus-white comparisons are descriptively favorable and the normal cornmeal comparison differs. Rat evidence and a processed human hydrolysate trial give general motor outcomes without a separate clinical postural-stability result. A bridge to the frozen posture endpoint remains unresolved.
